claims.text: Nearly equiatomic AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are high-entropy alloy nanoparticles.
The AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles possess a homogeneous atomic structure at room temperature.
In-situ aberration-corrected TEM with a dedicated heating stage can investigate the thermal behavior of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles at atomic resolution.
A controlled temperature ramp can be applied from room temperature to elevated temperature under high vacuum or an inert atmosphere.
The atomic lattice configuration and interatomic interfaces can be monitored during heating.
AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles will retain a relatively stable atomic lattice at elevated temperatures.
High configurational entropy contributes to the thermal stability of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
High configurational entropy lowers the driving force for diffusion-controlled coarsening.
High configurational entropy lowers the driving force for phase separation.
Suppression of coarsening and phase separation maintains nanoparticle structural integrity during heating.
Atomic-scale imaging will show minimal atomic reordering up to a high-temperature threshold.
Atomic-scale imaging will show minimal coarsening up to a high-temperature threshold.
Atomic-scale imaging will show minimal phase segregation up to a high-temperature threshold.
AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles will exhibit greater structural stability than similar non-high-entropy nanoparticles.
The room-temperature atomic structure provides the baseline for assessing heating-induced changes.
The predicted stability is conditional on near-equiatomic composition, a controlled atmosphere, and minimal electron-beam effects.
The predicted stability may not extend to different alloy compositions or oxidative environments.
Electron-beam-induced effects may influence the observed structural evolution.
